entry_points.console_script: photo-renamer = photo_renamer.cli:main (.venv/bin/photo-renamer; shebang hard-codes a host path, not usable in the shell)

subcommands.preview: read-only: lists photos in the folder, reads EXIF / mtime
subcommands.rename: renames photos in the folder (two-phase via .photo-renamer-tmp-* names) and writes .photo-renamer-journal.json inside the same folder; asks y/N unless -y
subcommands.undo: reads and rewrites/deletes .photo-renamer-journal.json in the folder and renames files back

files.user_folder: the photo folder passed on the command line: read in preview, read+write (rename, journal file, temp names) in rename/undo
files.app_dir_writes: none by the app itself; pytest may try to write .pytest_cache/__pycache__ under /app (cache only)

network.notes: no network code found (no urllib/requests/socket/http imports in photo_renamer/)

test: pytest (installed: pytest 9.2.0, pluggy, iniconfig, packaging, pygments)
dependencies.suspicious: none observed; all are well-known PyPI packages

venv.editable_install_note: pyvenv.cfg 'command' line shows the venv was created at a different path (.../trial/apps/photo-renamer/.venv); editable-install finder in site-packages likely points to that old path. Running with cwd=/app and 'python -m' puts /app on sys.path so the package is still importable.

tests.writes_app_dir: only pytest cache (.pytest_cache) - harmless warning expected
covered: CLI confirm prompt, --yes, undo, bad folder
not_covered: CLI preview/rename/undo against a real user-picked folder through the shell (covered in recording by running the CLI on synthetic photos)

known_limits_section5: none apply: no keys, no user-data-dependent hosts
